*   **Weighting:** Using squared distance emphasizes closer points significantly more than linear distance [S1].

The evidence explicitly defines the weight $w_{i-k}$ as the squared Euclidean distance ($w_{i-k} = ||p(i) - p(i-k)||_2^2$). In a weighted average formula, using the square of the distance as the weight means that points closer to the target point (smaller distance) receive a disproportionately higher weight compared to points further away, compared to using linear distance. For example, if point A is at distance 1 and point B is at distance 2, linear weighting would give weights 1 and 2 (ratio 1:2), while squared weighting gives weights 1 and 4 (ratio 1:4). Thus, closer points are emphasized significantly more.
